transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-15 10:00 PT | duration 72 mins | Location: All-hands (hybrid)
Attendees: Asha, Diego, Maya, Samir, Olivia, whole company tuning in

--- Summary (auto):
Asha opens with Q1 scoreboard, then hands to Tech Labs for three short demos. Brief discussion about an incident from early March and mitigations. Hiring and budget rebalancing called out; questions from eng and growth. Ends with next steps and links.

--- Topics raised (auto):
- Performance and cost: p50/p95/p99 trends, cost-per-token reductions
- New kernels & quantization tradeoffs
- Incident RCA: degraded KV cache under burst load
- DX roadmap and community outreach (templates, quickstarts)

--- Transcript body:
[00:00] Asha Patel (CEO): okay good morning everyone, uh thanks for joining this week, um we're gonna start the horizon review, keep this at a high level and then the Tech Labs team has some short demos so, Diego take it away with the scoreboard
[02:14] Diego Ramos (VP Product): yeah thanks Asha. Quick scoreboard: product usage up 23% q/q, hosted API token volume grew 18%. Cost-per-token down slightly from our December baseline, um we're seeing wins from caching and some manual kernel tweaks but it's not uniform across customers
[04:05] Maya Lin (Head of Eng): to add to that, the p99 has improved on steady state, but we had two spikes last month. they're addressed in the RCA that Samir will present. some of the edge cases were from cache eviction storms and a coupling with autoscaler cooldowns
[06:40] Samir Rao (Platform SE): yeah i'll show slides in a sec but short version — under certain prefix distributions our KV cache misses amplified and batching backpressure led to a queue that made p99 worse for a narrow class of requests. the rollout had canaries but not the specific sequence. we've added a guardrail that reduces batch size upper bound when eviction rate crosses threshold
[09:55] Audience (QA): question — was this customer-facing downtime or throttling?
[10:02] Samir Rao: Not downtime per se, more elevated latency and a handful of 500s for requests that hit the unlucky sequence. affected customers were on dedicated and some hosted tenants in the same GPU pool.
[11:30] Asha Patel: appreciation for the openness on RCA. Quick ask — Samir, can you include a short blurb for CSMs so they can proactively reach out to impacted accounts?
[11:58] Samir Rao: yes will do, i'll put a template in the internal incident playbook and share a copy
[13:20] Diego Ramos: moving to Tech Labs — we have three demos: 1) new KV heuristics that bias keep-alive for hot prefixes, 2) a 4-bit quantized kernel prototype for LLaMA-family weights which shows 1.6x throughput gains, 3) an adaptive batching controller that balances latency SLOs and cost targets
[15:02] Samir Rao: demo one first — this is a small change to eviction scoring where we take in an approximate prefix popularity estimator. in our sandbox we saw cold-start tail drop 12% and token cost down about 6% on chat workloads
[17:30] Crowd: (claps)
[18:00] Olivia Chen (DX): quick note, DX will add a recipe in the new SDK examples for the prefix caching pattern, with a sample config and annotated tradeoffs. we'll publish it this sprint
[19:45] Diego Ramos: demo two — the 4-bit kernel. important caveat: we saw some hallucination surface area increase in specific instruction-following prompts when we pushed aggressive quantization without matched calibration. quality regressions are small on average but present in corner cases
[21:10] Maya Lin: that's important — any break/fix plan for customers who see subtle generation drift?
[21:26] Samir Rao: yes we have an automatic fallback: route to a higher-precision variant if similarity score to an eval baseline exceeds threshold. it's part of the smart routing policies
[22:45] Audience (Engineer): are we unit-testing those fallback gates?
[23:10] Samir Rao: not full coverage yet, plan to add a harness with synthetic prompts. Diego will own the customer release notes
[25:00] Diego Ramos: demo three — adaptive batching controller. we ran a week-long canary and saw end-to-end token cost reduce 8% with negligible p95 impact, but p99 edged up slightly during bursts. suggestion: combine with the new KV guards and that yields a net win
[28:12] Asha Patel: okay thanks team. pivoting now to organizational notes — hiring: we've paused a handful of individual contributor reqs to redirect budget to automation and core platform reliability. people managers will get details in email
[30:20] Audience (Engineer): does this mean fewer IC ladders being opened?
[30:35] Maya Lin: for now yes on new senior IC hires in infra, but we still hire for strategic roles and critical customer coverage. this is temporary while we fund some cross-cutting automation work
[33:00] Jonah (Ops, guest): on incidents, a suggestion — can the autoscaler have a small safety headroom buffer to prevent oscillation? we've seen cooldowns align poorly with eviction patterns
[33:25] Samir Rao: that's in the mitigations list, we'll prototype a buffer and tune the cooldown window in staging
[35:50] Olivia Chen: community & open-source — we want to run a "starter app" contest to drive adoption and gather real-world patterns. prize and spotlight on site. intent is to get more varied prompt distributions in the wild
[36:50] Crowd: (enthusiastic)
[38:15] Asha Patel: leadership ask — more cross-functional time for small experiments. we'll allocate two "maker days" per quarter starting next month. engineers and product folks can pair and ship small infra or DX improvements
[40:40] Audience (Finance): question on cost targets — how tight are we on the unit economics goal for next quarter?
[40:58] Diego Ramos: we have a target to shave another 7% off cost per effective token by end of Q2. combination of caching, adaptive batching, compiler optimizations and selective quantization.
[43:10] Q&A (mixed): multiple micro-questions about SSO, audit logs, and SOC-2 timeline (somewhat noisy)
[45:15] Maya Lin: quick status — SOC 2 Type II prep is on track, control docs ready, we're scheduling the external audit in June.
[46:30] Asha Patel: empathy moment — shoutouts to the oncall and Platform team for handling the March incident. also want to surface that a few teammates are rotating to customer programs to accelerate real-world feedback
[48:00] Lila (Research): short update — we landed a prototype attention optimization that reduces memory for long sequences by about 18% in internal evals. still in research but promising for long-context customers
[50:30] Samir Rao: technical caveat — memory win helps but we need kernel work to translate to throughput on A100-like hardware; that's a near-term engineering task
[52:15] Audience (Sales): question about messaging to prospects about quantization and hallucination tradeoffs
[52:40] Diego Ramos: recommended messaging: be explicit — "we can enable aggressive quantization for throughput-sensitive workloads with automatic fallbacks; we monitor quality regressions and provide opt-out"
[54:10] Audience (Engineer): small nit — can the SDK surface quality metrics per request so customers can make smarter tradeoffs?
[54:35] Olivia Chen: yes that's a DX roadmap item, sampling quality metrics and surfacing as optional telemetry in the SDK is planned
[56:00] Asha Patel: wrapping up — reiterate focus: reliability (primary), measured performance wins (secondary), and community momentum (tertiary). we will be transparent on releases and incidents
[57:20] Diego Ramos: final ask: everyone check the roadmap board and react with thumbs where you can help or have a conflict
[58:40] Asha Patel: okay last thing, quick lightning recognition: 
[59:00] - Oncall team for March mitigation (shoutout)
[59:20] - Tech Labs for the 4-bit kernel prototype
[59:40] - DX for the upcoming SDK recipe
[60:10] Asha Patel: thanks all, we'll post recordings and the Tech Labs artifacts in the #all-hands channel, and follow-up threads for the action items. meeting adjourned.
